gaps: P0: nothing. P3: nothing strong (only a small 1831 etching of a Prinsenhof gate, #19). P5: nothing usable.
notes: #8 is a 1575 printing of the vol. 1 plate, dated to first publication, 1572. P2 alternative: #12 Chéreau colored view ‘c. 1720’ (dealer date, stylized and probably derivative). #14 Vrijdagmarkt wood engraving is captioned 1870, not 1830s; too close to the 1890s photochrom for a second P4. #17/#18 show the Hôtel de Cluny in Paris; #11 is a 19th-century pastiche; #10 is a plan. #19 (De Noter, 1831) skipped as weak; it could fill P3 if a weak view is preferred to a blank. P5 options #28 (1928 etching of a quay) and #29 (Willaert painting, 1908–38) are weak or loosely dated. P6 alternatives: #33 (three towers from the Gravensteen, but cranes) and #32 (three towers from St. Michael’s Bridge, dark).
